_what: How tools/start-a-place makes and starts one Trillion place (do-work/start-a-place.mjs). The place config it writes is the engine's (trillion-rust src/native_entry/place.rs, its module doc): listen, accounts, place_key_file, public_origin, report, sign_in, sign_up, new_accounts, and optionally access, router and default_places. `files` are the names it gives the config, the key file and the serve log inside the place folder. `program` is the engine's command-line program, looked for on the PATH when the request names none. `key_bytes` is the size of a place key (trillion-rust src/held_values/root.json `place_key_bytes`); the key file holds them as base64 on one line, made once and never overwritten or read here. `private_file_mode` is the mode of the key file and the config. `origin_scheme` is the only scheme a public origin may have. `most_places` is how many places one list of default_places may name (the shipped `access:places` row a new account has, trillion-rust src/account/places/settings.json). `place_id_hex_length` is a place id's length (its public key, lowercase hex). `this_place` is the word a default_places list may hold for the place being started, whose id is known only once its key is made. `settle_ms` is how long the serve is watched after it starts: a place that stops within it is refused with its log's last lines (`log_lines_told`). `id_timeout_ms` bounds `place id`. `report`, `sign_in` and `sign_up` are the values used for each field the request leaves out, the engine's own test place's (trillion-rust tests/place_router.rs); `report.reach` left out is the public origin. `new_accounts` names the starting rows file used when the request gives none: read-data/new-accounts.json, a byte copy of trillion-rust tests/fixtures/new-accounts.json, the product's own rows. `computer` names the files on a computer the start and the update step write: the place config, the service unit, the product settings file (named to the engine in the launch setting `product_settings_setting`, trillion-rust src/account_files/identity.json `launch_setting`; its values are read-data/`product_settings`), the folder each update keeps its backup in (`backups`, one folder per update holding `new/` and `old/`), and `settle_seconds`, how long an update waits after the restart before it reads whether the service is active. `release_feed` names the feed file used when the request gives none (read-data/release-feed.json); a request's `release_feed: null` writes none. The program of a release the feed adopts is `program`.
